 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. India and New Zealand meet again in the second match of the five-match T20I series at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday, October 24. The visitors began the series with a thrilling win and will now try to move 2-0 ahead.
 New Zealand scored 225 in the opening game, but Shreyas Iyer and his teammates chased it down with four wickets in hand and two balls to spare.

 Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma gave the chase a flying start with an opening stand of 93. Samson made 67 off 33 balls, and Naman Dhir finished unbeaten on 42 off only 15 deliveries to carry India home.
 New Zealand vs. India 2nd T20I live stream and TV channel
 Here is how to watch the second T20I in India, using the broadcast details from the first game.
 TV channel: Sony Sports Network.
 Live stream: Sony LIV
 Viewers in India can follow the match live on Sony Sports Network, while the Sony LIV app and website will carry the live stream.
 Add The Sporting News as a preferred news source 
 What time does the New Zealand vs. India 2nd T20I start?
 The second T20I will be played at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday, October 24. Play is scheduled to begin at 8:00 PM local time (NZDT), which is 12:30 PM IST for viewers in India.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement New Zealand vs. India 2nd T20I team news, lineups 
 There should be no need for forced changes in New Zealand's side this early in the series, so they are likely to stay with the same group.
 New Zealand predicted XI: Tim Seifert (wk), Finn Allen, Devon Conway, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Matt Henry, Lockie Ferguson, Jacob Duffy.
 Ishan Kishan will miss Saturday's game with a groin strain, and that opens the door for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to come back into India's line-up. The teenager sat out the T20Is against West Indies and Thursday's series opener, so this would be a return to the side.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement If Sooryavanshi replaces Kishan as expected, he will probably open alongside Abhishek, with Samson dropping to No.3. That has generally been India's set-up when these three play together.
 India predicted XI: Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh, Mayank Yadav.
